craft_notes: Sthāyin: raudra-śṛṅgāra of reddening; vyabhicāri rāga at rush-to-red. Sanskrit-first: raktatā-rūṣ (RUSH-TO-REDNESS — kept rushing); ghṛṇā double held (LOATHING + COMPASSION both, per UNC — never picked); nanu (PRAYER-PARTICLE per UNC — kept). Rows: 9 (outer-emit/bliss-taste/rush triple — emission, taste, rush), 1 (‘red-drinking rite’ closes — the rite named last). Close: ‘past loathing of the red-drinking rite’. Rupture: em-dash (rush stated, then its prayer — redness rushed, loathing prayed past). Rejected: picking loathing-vs-compassion — killed: held double per UNC; ‘crimson’ for red — killed: red kept raw (raudra). Read aloud: WHEN in-THE-out-er e-MIT, IN-utt-most BLISS-taste, YOU-rush TO-red-NESS — … THEN, RED-god-DESS, MAKE-me PAST-loath-ing OF the-RED-drink-ing-RITE.

lines: When in the outer emit, in utmost bliss-taste, You rush to redness —
then, red goddess, make me past loathing of the red-drinking rite.
l4.sanskrit_cite: yadā tatraiva tvaṃ bhajasi rabhasād raktimayatām | kriyād raktāpānakramaghaṭitagoṣṭhīgataghṛṇam

c1_essence: Rush-to-redness resorted; past-loathing prayed in red conclave.
